docs.title: Energy Landscapes
docs.text:
intro · An energy E(x) defines a density p(x) proportional to exp(-E(x)); evaluate it and its force field -grad E.

Run it:

python examples/00-foundations/01-energy/01-energy-landscapes/main.py

"""Energy functions: an energy E(x) defines a density p(x) proportional to exp(-E(x)).

Each model maps points of shape (N, 2) to energies (N,); the negative gradient
-grad E is the score of the model density (physicists call it the force), and it
is the direction every gradient-based sampler follows. Lower energy means higher
probability. Built with prediction_type=("energy", "score"), one call returns
both; the analytic models have closed-form scores.
"""

import torch

from torchebm.core import GaussianModel, DoubleWellModel, RosenbrockModel

models = {
    "gaussian": GaussianModel(
        mean=torch.zeros(2), cov=torch.eye(2), prediction_type=("energy", "score")
    ),
    "double_well": DoubleWellModel(
        barrier_height=2.0, prediction_type=("energy", "score")
    ),
    "rosenbrock": RosenbrockModel(prediction_type=("energy", "score")),
}

xs = torch.linspace(-3.0, 3.0, 25)
grid = torch.stack(torch.meshgrid(xs, xs, indexing="xy"), dim=-1).reshape(-1, 2)

for name, model in models.items():
    energy, score = model(grid)
    print(f"{name:12s} E in [{energy.min():.2f}, {energy.max():.2f}]   "
          f"mean |score| = {score.norm(dim=1).mean():.2f}")

docs.title: Custom Energies
docs.text:
intro · Subclass BaseModel with any differentiable map (N, d) -> (N,); built with prediction_type, its call returns the energy, the autograd score, or both.

Run it:

python examples/00-foundations/01-energy/02-custom-energy/main.py

"""Custom energies: a differentiable BaseModel subclass has an autograd score and works with every sampler.

    E(x) defines p(x) proportional to exp(-E(x)); anything that maps (N, d) -> (N,)
    and is differentiable is a valid energy, analytic or neural.

Built with prediction_type=("energy", "score"), the call returns the energy and
the autograd score -grad E together. The ring's minimum is the circle |x| = 2:
zero score on the ring, a strong pull outside.
"""

import torch
from torch import nn

from torchebm.core import BaseModel, GaussianModel


class RingEnergy(BaseModel):
    def __init__(self, radius=2.0, width=0.25, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.radius, self.width = radius, width

    def forward(self, x):
        return (x.norm(dim=-1) - self.radius) ** 2 / (2 * self.width**2)


class MLP(BaseModel):
    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(2, 64), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(64, 1),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x).squeeze(-1)


points = torch.tensor([[2.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0], [3.0, 0.0]])

for name, model in {
    "ring": RingEnergy(prediction_type=("energy", "score")),
    "gaussian": GaussianModel(
        mean=torch.zeros(2), cov=torch.eye(2), prediction_type=("energy", "score")
    ),
    "mlp (untrained)": MLP(prediction_type=("energy", "score")),
}.items():
    energy, score = model(points)
    print(f"{name:16s} E = {[round(e, 2) for e in energy.tolist()]}"
          f"   |score| = {[round(s, 2) for s in score.norm(dim=1).tolist()]}")

docs.title: Dataset Gallery
docs.text:
intro · The eight synthetic 2D targets: one constructor contract, standard benchmarks from the flow and EBM literature.

Run it:

python examples/00-foundations/02-datasets/01-dataset-gallery/main.py

"""Synthetic 2D benchmarks: the standard toy targets used across flow and EBM papers.

Each dataset is a torch Dataset generating (n_samples, 2) points on construction;
get_data() returns the full tensor for direct batching, and len(dataset) and
dataset[i] work as usual. All share seed, device and dtype, plus per-shape knobs
(n_samples, noise, std, radius, ...; the grid counts points per dimension).
"""

import torch

from torchebm.datasets import (
    CheckerboardDataset,
    CircleDataset,
    EightGaussiansDataset,
    GaussianMixtureDataset,
    GridDataset,
    PinwheelDataset,
    SwissRollDataset,
    TwoMoonsDataset,
)

N, SEED = 2048, 0

datasets = {
    "gaussian_mixture": GaussianMixtureDataset(n_samples=N, seed=SEED),
    "eight_gaussians": EightGaussiansDataset(n_samples=N, seed=SEED),
    "two_moons": TwoMoonsDataset(n_samples=N, noise=0.05, seed=SEED),
    "swiss_roll": SwissRollDataset(n_samples=N, seed=SEED),
    "circle": CircleDataset(n_samples=N, seed=SEED),
    "checkerboard": CheckerboardDataset(n_samples=N, seed=SEED),
    "pinwheel": PinwheelDataset(n_samples=N, seed=SEED),
    "grid": GridDataset(n_samples_per_dim=45, seed=SEED),
}

for name, dataset in datasets.items():
    x = dataset.get_data()
    extent = x.abs().max().item()
    print(f"{name:17s} shape {tuple(x.shape)}   mean {x.mean(0).round(decimals=2).tolist()}"
          f"   std {x.std(0).round(decimals=2).tolist()}   extent {extent:.2f}")

print("len(two_moons) =", len(datasets["two_moons"]))

docs.title: Scheduler Anatomy
docs.text:
intro · Linear, cosine, and exponential schedules, and how a sampler advances a scheduled parameter per step.

Run it:

python examples/00-foundations/03-schedulers/01-scheduler-anatomy/main.py

"""Schedulers: time-varying hyperparameters that samplers advance automatically.

Any parameter registered as Schedulable (step_size, noise_scale, ...) accepts a
float or a BaseScheduler; the sampler calls step() once per iteration. A
scheduler is a stateful value: step() advances it, get_value() reads it. The
annealed Langevin run below decays its step size along a cosine, driven by the
sampler itself.
"""

import os

import torch

from torchebm.core import (
    CosineScheduler,
    ExponentialDecayScheduler,
    GaussianModel,
    LinearScheduler,
)
from torchebm.samplers import LangevinDynamics

SMOKE = os.getenv("TORCHEBM_SMOKE") == "1"
N_STEPS = 20 if SMOKE else 500

schedulers = {
    "linear 1.0 -> 0.1": LinearScheduler(start_value=1.0, end_value=0.1, n_steps=5),
    "cosine 1.0 -> 0.1": CosineScheduler(start_value=1.0, end_value=0.1, n_steps=5),
    "exp decay x0.5": ExponentialDecayScheduler(start_value=1.0, decay_rate=0.5),
}
for name, scheduler in schedulers.items():
    values = [round(scheduler.step(), 3) for _ in range(5)]
    print(f"{name:20s} {values}")

model = GaussianModel(mean=torch.zeros(2), cov=torch.tensor([[1.0, 0.8], [0.8, 1.0]]))
sampler = LangevinDynamics(
    step_size=CosineScheduler(start_value=0.05, end_value=0.005, n_steps=N_STEPS),
    noise_scale=1.0,
)
samples = sampler(model, torch.randn(2000, 2), n_steps=N_STEPS)
print("annealed samples:", tuple(samples.shape))
print("recovered covariance:\n", torch.cov(samples.T).round(decimals=2))

docs.title: Interpolant Anatomy
docs.text:
intro · The path x_t = alpha(t) x1 + sigma(t) x0 and its conditional velocity, for the linear, cosine, and VP schedules.

Run it:

python examples/00-foundations/04-interpolants/01-interpolant-anatomy/main.py

"""Interpolants: the time path x_t = alpha(t) x1 + sigma(t) x0 between noise and data.

    x0 ~ N(0, I) (source), x1 ~ data (target); the conditional velocity
    u_t = d_alpha(t) x1 + d_sigma(t) x0 is the regression target of flow matching.

alpha rises 0 -> 1 (data weight) and sigma falls 1 -> 0 (noise weight), so the
endpoints are exact for every schedule: t=0 recovers x0, t=1 recovers x1. The
call draws the path point and its conditional velocity.
"""

import torch

from torchebm.interpolants import (
    CosineInterpolant,
    LinearInterpolant,
    VariancePreservingInterpolant,
)

interpolants = {
    "linear": LinearInterpolant(),
    "cosine": CosineInterpolant(),
    "vp": VariancePreservingInterpolant(),
}

t = torch.tensor([0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0])
for name, interpolant in interpolants.items():
    alpha, d_alpha = interpolant.compute_alpha_t(t)
    sigma, d_sigma = interpolant.compute_sigma_t(t)
    print(f"{name:7s} alpha(t) = {alpha.round(decimals=3).tolist()}"
          f"   sigma(t) = {sigma.round(decimals=3).tolist()}")

torch.manual_seed(0)
x0 = torch.randn(4096, 2)
x1 = torch.randn(4096, 2) * 0.1 + 2.0
for name, interpolant in interpolants.items():
    t_mid = torch.full((4096,), 0.5)
    x_t, u_t = interpolant(x0, x1, t_mid)
    print(f"{name:7s} at t=0.5: E|x_t| = {x_t.norm(dim=1).mean():.2f}"
          f"   E|u_t| = {u_t.norm(dim=1).mean():.2f}")

interpolant = LinearInterpolant()
x_t0, _ = interpolant(x0, x1, torch.zeros(4096))
x_t1, _ = interpolant(x0, x1, torch.ones(4096))
print("endpoint error:", (x_t0 - x0).abs().max().item(), (x_t1 - x1).abs().max().item())

docs.title: Langevin Dynamics 101
docs.text:
intro · Sample a 2D energy with Langevin; trade step size against noise.

Run it:

python examples/10-sampling/01-mcmc/01-langevin-101/main.py

"""Langevin Dynamics: sample a 2D energy by descending its gradient with noise.

    x <- x - step_size * grad E(x) + sqrt(2 * step_size) * noise_scale * eps

The target is a correlated Gaussian, E(x) = 1/2 x^T Sigma^-1 x. The call runs
2000 independent chains as one batch and returns their final points.
"""

import os

import torch

from torchebm.core import GaussianModel
from torchebm.samplers import LangevinDynamics

SMOKE = os.getenv("TORCHEBM_SMOKE") == "1"
N_STEPS = 20 if SMOKE else 500

model = GaussianModel(mean=torch.zeros(2), cov=torch.tensor([[1.0, 0.8], [0.8, 1.0]]))
sampler = LangevinDynamics(step_size=0.02, noise_scale=1.0)
samples = sampler(model, torch.randn(2000, 2), n_steps=N_STEPS)

print("samples:", tuple(samples.shape))
print("mean:", samples.mean(0).round(decimals=2).tolist())
print("recovered covariance:\n", torch.cov(samples.T).round(decimals=2))

docs.title: HMC 101
docs.text:
intro · Hamiltonian Monte Carlo on a correlated Gaussian; trade leapfrog steps against gradient cost and chain autocorrelation.

Run it:

python examples/10-sampling/01-mcmc/02-hmc-101/main.py

"""Hamiltonian Monte Carlo: long, informed proposals with Metropolis acceptance.

HMC simulates Hamiltonian dynamics with a leapfrog integrator for a few steps,
then accepts or rejects; longer trajectories decorrelate more per proposal but
cost more gradient evaluations. On a strongly correlated Gaussian (hard for
plain Langevin), 2 leapfrog steps behave like a timid random walk while 50 buy
nearly independent proposals at 25x the gradient cost per transition; the
lag-1 autocorrelation of the chains measures the trade.
"""

import os

import torch

from torchebm.core import GaussianModel
from torchebm.samplers import HamiltonianMonteCarlo

SMOKE = os.getenv("TORCHEBM_SMOKE") == "1"
N_STEPS = 20 if SMOKE else 300

model = GaussianModel(mean=torch.zeros(2), cov=torch.tensor([[1.0, 0.95], [0.95, 1.0]]))
x0 = torch.randn(1000, 2)

for n_leapfrog in (2, 10, 50):
    sampler = HamiltonianMonteCarlo(step_size=0.1, n_leapfrog_steps=n_leapfrog)
    trajectory = sampler(model, x0, n_steps=N_STEPS, return_trajectory=True)
    samples = trajectory[:, -1]
    x = trajectory[:, N_STEPS // 2 :, 0]
    x = x - x.mean()
    autocorrelation = (x[:, 1:] * x[:, :-1]).mean() / x.pow(2).mean()
    print(f"n_leapfrog={n_leapfrog:3d}  lag-1 autocorrelation {autocorrelation:.2f}"
          f"   recovered cov(0,1) = {torch.cov(samples.T)[0, 1]:.2f}  (target 0.95)")

docs.title: Parallel Chains
docs.text:
intro · 10,000 vectorized Langevin chains in one call; population statistics without long single-chain runs.

Run it:

python examples/10-sampling/01-mcmc/03-parallel-chains/main.py

"""Parallel chains: samplers are vectorized over the batch dimension.

The 10,000 Langevin chains below advance as one tensor program, and on a GPU
the same call runs millions of chains. Population statistics come from many
parallel chains at once; contrastive divergence draws its negatives the same
way. The target is a double well whose first coordinate has two symmetric
modes, at -b and +b.
"""

import os

import torch

from torchebm.core import DoubleWellModel
from torchebm.samplers import LangevinDynamics

SMOKE = os.getenv("TORCHEBM_SMOKE") == "1"
N_STEPS = 20 if SMOKE else 500
N_CHAINS = 10_000

model = DoubleWellModel(barrier_height=2.0)
sampler = LangevinDynamics(step_size=0.01, noise_scale=1.0)
samples = sampler(model, torch.randn(N_CHAINS, 2), n_steps=N_STEPS)

left = (samples[:, 0] < 0).float().mean()
print("samples:", tuple(samples.shape))
print(f"basin occupancy: left {left:.1%} / right {1 - left:.1%}  (symmetric target: 50/50)")
print(f"mean energy: {model(samples).mean():.2f}")

docs.title: Integrator Comparison
docs.text:
intermediate · Euler, Heun, and RK4 against the exact solution of a harmonic oscillator; measure order of accuracy directly.

Run it:

python examples/10-sampling/02-integrators/01-integrator-comparison/main.py

"""Integrators: order of accuracy, measured against an exact ODE solution.

    dx/dt = A x with A = [[0, 1], [-1, 0]] is a harmonic oscillator whose exact
    solution is a rotation; halving the step should shrink the error by 2^order.

The registry constructs integrators by name, and samplers accept the same
names through integrator="...". Over one full revolution Euler drifts off the
circle, Heun gains two orders, RK4 four.
"""

import math

import torch

from torchebm.integrators import get_integrator

A = torch.tensor([[0.0, 1.0], [-1.0, 0.0]])
T = 2 * math.pi
x0 = torch.randn(256, 2)


def drift(x, t):
    return x @ A.T


def exact(t):
    c, s = math.cos(t), math.sin(t)
    return x0 @ torch.tensor([[c, -s], [s, c]]).T


for name, order in (("euler_maruyama", 1), ("heun", 2), ("rk4", 4)):
    errors = []
    for n_steps in (100, 200):
        integrator = get_integrator(name)
        t = torch.linspace(0.0, T, n_steps + 1)
        xT = integrator.integrate(
            state={"x": x0.clone()},
            step_size=t[1] - t[0],
            n_steps=n_steps,
            drift=drift,
            t=t,
        )["x"]
        errors.append((xT - exact(T)).norm(dim=1).mean().item())
    ratio = errors[0] / errors[1]
    print(f"{name:15s} error {errors[0]:.2e} -> {errors[1]:.2e} on halved step"
          f"   ratio {ratio:5.1f}  (theory ~{2**order})")

docs.title: FlowSampler ODE 101
docs.text:
intermediate · Integrate a closed-form velocity field from noise to a Gaussian target; study steps vs fidelity without training.

Run it:

python examples/10-sampling/03-flow/01-flow-sampler-ode/main.py

"""FlowSampler: integrate a velocity field from noise to data, no training needed.

For a Gaussian target N(mu, s^2 I) under the linear path x_t = t x1 + (1-t) x0,
the marginal velocity is closed-form:

    u(x, t) = mu + (t s^2 - (1 - t)) / (t^2 s^2 + (1 - t)^2) * (x - t mu)

so the sampler's mechanics can be studied in isolation from learning. More
steps mean less discretization error; integrator="heun" or the adaptive
"dopri5" collapse the error at few steps, and trained velocity models (see
20-training) plug in identically.
"""

import torch
from torch import nn

from torchebm.samplers import FlowSampler

MU = torch.tensor([2.0, -1.0])
S = 0.5


class AnalyticVelocity(nn.Module):
    def forward(self, x, t, **kwargs):
        t = torch.as_tensor(t, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device).view(-1, 1)
        var = t**2 * S**2 + (1 - t) ** 2
        return MU + (t * S**2 - (1 - t)) / var * (x - t * MU)


model = AnalyticVelocity()
sampler = FlowSampler(interpolant="linear", integrator="euler")

torch.manual_seed(0)
x0 = torch.randn(8192, 2)
for n_steps in (2, 8, 64):
    samples = sampler(model, x0, n_steps=n_steps)
    mean_err = (samples.mean(0) - MU).norm()
    std_err = (samples.std(0) - S).abs().max()
    print(f"n_steps={n_steps:3d}  mean error {mean_err:.3f}   std error {std_err:.3f}")

docs.title: CD-k on Two Moons
docs.text:
intermediate · Train an energy network with Contrastive Divergence and Langevin negatives.

Run it:

python examples/20-training/01-mcmc-losses/01-cd-k/main.py

"""Contrastive Divergence: train an energy net so data sits in low-energy regions.

CD pushes E down on real data and up on short-run MCMC "negatives" from the model:
the sampler draws them from the current model with k Langevin steps started at
the data batch (CD-10 here), and the loss is mean E(data) - mean E(negatives).
"""

import os

import torch
from torch import nn

from torchebm.core import BaseModel
from torchebm.datasets import TwoMoonsDataset
from torchebm.losses import ContrastiveDivergenceLoss
from torchebm.samplers import LangevinDynamics

SMOKE = os.getenv("TORCHEBM_SMOKE") == "1"
N_STEPS = 20 if SMOKE else 1000


class MLP(BaseModel):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(2, 128), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, 128), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, 1),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x).squeeze(-1)


data = TwoMoonsDataset(n_samples=3000, noise=0.05, seed=0).get_data()

model = MLP()
sampler = LangevinDynamics(step_size=0.1, noise_scale=1.0)
loss_fn = ContrastiveDivergenceLoss()
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)

for step in range(N_STEPS):
    batch = data[torch.randint(len(data), (256,))]
    negatives = sampler(model, batch, n_steps=10)
    loss = loss_fn(model(batch), model(negatives))
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    if step % 200 == 0:
        print(f"step {step:4d}  loss {loss.item():+.3f}")

docs.title: Persistent CD
docs.text:
intermediate · CD with a replay buffer: negatives resume across updates and explore beyond k Langevin steps.

Run it:

python examples/20-training/01-mcmc-losses/02-persistent-cd/main.py

"""Persistent CD: negative chains resume from a replay buffer across updates.

Chains that persist across updates explore the model distribution far beyond
k Langevin steps, at identical per-step cost to CD-k. The buffer is the only
difference from cd-k: chains start from it and their end points go back in,
with 5% of each draw restarting from noise (Du and Mordatch, 2019) so the pool
keeps exploring. A healthy run drives E(neg) - E(data) toward zero: the chains
reach the model's own typical set, so the negative phase of the gradient is
less biased than with chains restarted at the data. BaseTrainer(model,
optimizer, loss_fn, sampler=sampler, buffer=buffer) runs the same loop.
"""

import os

import torch
from torch import nn

from torchebm.core import BaseModel
from torchebm.datasets import TwoMoonsDataset
from torchebm.losses import ContrastiveDivergenceLoss
from torchebm.samplers import LangevinDynamics
from torchebm.utils import ReplayBuffer

SMOKE = os.getenv("TORCHEBM_SMOKE") == "1"
N_STEPS = 20 if SMOKE else 1000


class MLP(BaseModel):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(2, 128), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, 128), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, 1),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x).squeeze(-1)


data = TwoMoonsDataset(n_samples=3000, noise=0.05, seed=0).get_data()

model = MLP()
sampler = LangevinDynamics(step_size=0.1, noise_scale=1.0)
loss_fn = ContrastiveDivergenceLoss()
buffer = ReplayBuffer(capacity=8192, sample_shape=(2,))
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)

for step in range(N_STEPS):
    batch = data[torch.randint(len(data), (256,))]
    negatives = sampler(model, buffer.sample(256), n_steps=10)
    buffer.add(negatives)
    loss = loss_fn(model(batch), model(negatives))
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    if step % 200 == 0:
        gap = model(negatives).mean() - model(batch).mean()
        print(f"step {step:4d}  loss {loss.item():+.3f}  E(neg) - E(data) = {gap.item():+.3f}")

docs.title: Denoising Score Matching
docs.text:
intermediate · Train an energy on two moons with no MCMC: perturb, match the denoising score, then sample the result with Langevin.

Run it:

python examples/20-training/02-score-matching/01-denoising-score-matching/main.py

"""Denoising Score Matching: train an energy without any MCMC sampling.

DSM (Vincent, 2011) perturbs data with Gaussian noise and matches the model
score to the denoising direction, the score of the perturbation kernel
-noise / sigma; no negatives, no Hessian trace. sigma sets the smoothing
bandwidth: the model learns the score of the noise-convolved data density, so
too large blurs the moons and too small is noisy.

The model returns its energy and its score from one call: the loss consumes
the score, the diagnostics read the energy, and the Langevin sampler picks the
score again. The trained energy separates data from off-manifold points and,
unlike the pure regression it was trained by, is still an EBM the same sampler
used for CD models draws from.
"""

import os

import torch
from torch import nn

from torchebm.core import BaseModel
from torchebm.datasets import TwoMoonsDataset
from torchebm.losses import DenoisingScoreMatchingLoss
from torchebm.samplers import LangevinDynamics

SMOKE = os.getenv("TORCHEBM_SMOKE") == "1"
N_STEPS = 20 if SMOKE else 2000
SAMPLE_STEPS = 20 if SMOKE else 500


class MLP(BaseModel):
    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(2, 128), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, 128), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, 1),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x).squeeze(-1)


data = TwoMoonsDataset(n_samples=3000, noise=0.05, seed=0).get_data()

model = MLP(prediction_type=("energy", "score"))
loss_fn = DenoisingScoreMatchingLoss()
sigma = 0.1
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)

for step in range(N_STEPS):
    batch = data[torch.randint(len(data), (256,))]
    noise = torch.randn_like(batch)
    _, score = model(batch + sigma * noise)
    loss = loss_fn(score, -noise / sigma)
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    if step % 400 == 0:
        print(f"step {step:4d}  loss {loss.item():.3f}")

x_random = torch.rand(2000, 2) * 4 - torch.tensor([1.5, 1.0])
with torch.no_grad():
    energy_data, _ = model(data)
    energy_random, _ = model(x_random)
print(f"E(data) = {energy_data.mean():.2f}   E(random box) = {energy_random.mean():.2f}")

sampler = LangevinDynamics(step_size=0.01, noise_scale=0.3)
samples = sampler(model, torch.randn(2000, 2), n_steps=SAMPLE_STEPS)
print("sampled from the DSM energy:", tuple(samples.shape))

docs.title: Equilibrium Matching in 2D
docs.text:
intermediate · Train a time-invariant field and an explicit potential with EquilibriumMatchingLoss; sample the field by ODE integration and by fixed-point iteration, and the potential by descent with optional repulsion.

Run it:

python examples/20-training/03-equilibrium-matching/01-equilibrium-matching-2d/main.py

"""Equilibrium Matching in 2D: one time-invariant field, two ways to sample it.

EqM trains a time-invariant model toward c(t) u_t, the path velocity from noise
to data scaled by a decay that vanishes at the data. This example trains two
models on two moons:

  - implicit: an MLP outputting the field f(x). It declares no
    prediction_type, so FlowSampler integrates it as the velocity, and
    GradientDescentSampler applies the same update x <- x + eta f(x) for more
    steps, iterating toward the field's attractors. The field is not
    constrained to be the gradient of an energy.
  - explicit (EqM-E): an MLP outputting a scalar energy E(x), trained through
    its score -grad E, so its field is a gradient by construction. Sample by
    descending E; wrap it in InteractionModel for diverse (repulsive)
    sampling.

The diverse coda starts 64 chains from one seed: plain gradient descent
collapses them to one point, the repulsive W spreads them along the low-energy
manifold. InteractionModel wraps an energy, so the explicit model switches to
its energy view and the sampler differentiates E(x) - W(x) itself; strength
keeps the per-step repulsion 2*s*B*dt/sigma_w^2 well below 1 (stable) yet
strong enough to overcome the pull to a single point.
"""

import os

import torch
from torch import nn

from torchebm.core import BaseModel
from torchebm.datasets import TwoMoonsDataset
from torchebm.interpolants import LinearInterpolant
from torchebm.losses import EquilibriumMatchingLoss
from torchebm.models import InteractionModel
from torchebm.samplers import FlowSampler, GradientDescentSampler

SMOKE = os.getenv("TORCHEBM_SMOKE") == "1"
N_STEPS = 20 if SMOKE else 2000
N_GEN = 128 if SMOKE else 2000


class MLP(nn.Module):
    """f(x) -> R^2; EqM is time-invariant, so the sampler's t is unused."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(2, 256), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 256), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 2),
        )

    def forward(self, x, t=None, **kwargs):
        return self.net(x)


class EnergyMLP(BaseModel):
    """E(x) -> R; built with prediction_type="score" the call returns -grad E."""

    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(2, 256), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 256), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 1, bias=False),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x).squeeze(-1)


def train(model):
    """Regress the model's output onto c(t) u_t along the linear path."""
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    data = TwoMoonsDataset(n_samples=4000, noise=0.05, seed=0).get_data()
    path = LinearInterpolant()
    loss_fn = EquilibriumMatchingLoss()
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    for _ in range(N_STEPS):
        x1 = data[torch.randint(len(data), (256,))]
        x0 = torch.randn_like(x1)
        t = torch.rand(len(x1))
        x_t, u_t = path(x0, x1, t)
        loss = loss_fn(model(x_t), u_t, t)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
    return data


def median_dist(samples, data):
    """Median distance from each sample to the nearest data point."""
    return torch.cdist(samples, data).min(dim=1).values.median().item()


model = MLP()
data = train(model)
x0 = torch.randn(N_GEN, 2)

samples_ode = FlowSampler(integrator="euler")(model, x0, n_steps=100)
samples_gd = GradientDescentSampler(step_size=0.05)(model, x0, n_steps=200)

print(f"implicit + ODE   median dist to data: {median_dist(samples_ode, data):.3f}")
print(f"implicit + GD    median dist to data: {median_dist(samples_gd, data):.3f}")

energy_model = EnergyMLP(prediction_type="score")
train(energy_model)
samples_energy = GradientDescentSampler(step_size=0.02)(energy_model, x0, n_steps=300)
print(f"explicit + GD    median dist to data: {median_dist(samples_energy, data):.3f}")

x_seed = torch.tensor([0.5, 1.6]) + 1e-3 * torch.randn(64, 2)
energy_model.prediction_type = "energy"
interaction_model = InteractionModel(energy_model, sigma_w=4.5, strength=0.5)
samples_repulsive = GradientDescentSampler(step_size=0.01)(interaction_model, x_seed, n_steps=200)
samples_plain = GradientDescentSampler(step_size=0.01)(energy_model, x_seed, n_steps=200)
spread = lambda s: s.std(dim=0).mean().item()
print(f"diverse coda spread   with W: {spread(samples_repulsive):.3f}   without W: {spread(samples_plain):.3f}")

docs.title: Energy Matching in 2D
docs.text:
intermediate · Reproduce the paper's two-moons experiment: a scalar potential trained with OT flow warm-up plus contrastive sharpening, sampled in one temperature-scheduled SDE sweep.

Run it:

python examples/20-training/04-energy-matching/01-energy-matching-2d/main.py

"""Energy Matching: one scalar potential for OT transport and Boltzmann sampling.

EM (arXiv:2504.10612) trains a time-independent potential V(x) in two phases:
a warm-up where -grad V regresses onto minibatch-OT displacements, then a joint
phase that adds contrastive divergence with temperature-scheduled Langevin
negatives, sharpening exp(-V/eps_max) near the data. Generation is one SDE
sweep: deterministic transport below tau*, a Langevin ramp up to eps_max.

The loop is the standard one: couple, interpolate, call the model, loss. The
model returns (V(x), -grad V(x)) from one call, so the flow term, the energies
of the contrastive term and the samplers all read the same network. Sinkhorn
OT pairs each batch in milliseconds at near-exact quality (reg=0.01;
ExactOTCoupling is exact but ~0.5 s per step). The negatives come half from
noise, chains sweeping the temperature profile eps(t), and half from data,
chains held at eps_max; the flow term is gated at tau* (flow_weight_cutoff).

This reproduces the paper's 2D toy experiment (two moons; tau*=0.8,
eps_max=0.15, 200-step Langevin negatives, dt=0.01, lambda_cd=2.0, lr=1e-4,
20000 flow + 2000 joint steps, 0.1 smoothing noise on x_t, plain CD without
trim/clamp). A healthy run populates both moons ~50/50 with samples hugging
the manifold (median distance ~0.1; the data itself measures ~0.03). A GPU is
recommended (~7 minutes end to end; CPU is much slower).
"""

import math
import os

import torch
from torch import nn

from torchebm.core import BaseModel, TemperatureScheduler
from torchebm.couplings import SinkhornCoupling
from torchebm.datasets import TwoMoonsDataset
from torchebm.interpolants import LinearInterpolant
from torchebm.losses import EnergyMatchingLoss
from torchebm.samplers import LangevinDynamics


class MLP(BaseModel):
    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(2, 256), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 256), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 256), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 1),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x).squeeze(-1)


def progress(label, step, total, loss):
    """Inline terminal progress bar (stdlib only)."""
    if step % 100 and step != total - 1:
        return
    bar = "=" * int(30 * (step + 1) / total)
    end = "\n" if step == total - 1 else ""
    print(
        f"\r{label} [{bar:<30}] {step + 1:5d}/{total}  loss {loss.item():.4f}",
        end=end, flush=True,
    )


SMOKE = os.getenv("TORCHEBM_SMOKE") == "1"
FLOW_STEPS, JOINT_STEPS = (20, 5) if SMOKE else (20000, 2000)
LANGEVIN_STEPS = 10 if SMOKE else 200
SWEEP_STEPS = 20 if SMOKE else 200
EPS_MAX, TAU_STAR, DT = 0.15, 0.8, 0.01

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
data = TwoMoonsDataset(n_samples=8000, noise=0.05, seed=0, device=device).get_data()

model = MLP(prediction_type=("energy", "score")).to(device)
coupling = SinkhornCoupling(reg=0.01)
path = LinearInterpolant()
loss_fn = EnergyMatchingLoss(lambda_cd=2.0, cd_trim_fraction=0.0, cd_clamp=None)
langevin_sweep = LangevinDynamics(
    step_size=DT,
    noise_scale=TemperatureScheduler(
        epsilon_max=EPS_MAX, tau_star=TAU_STAR, n_steps=LANGEVIN_STEPS
    ),
)
langevin_hold = LangevinDynamics(step_size=DT, noise_scale=math.sqrt(EPS_MAX))
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-4)


def compute_loss(x1, contrastive):
    x0, x1 = coupling(torch.randn_like(x1), x1)
    t = torch.rand(len(x1), device=device)
    x_t, u_t = path(x0, x1, t)
    x_t = x_t + 0.1 * torch.randn_like(x_t)
    _, score = model(x_t)
    if not contrastive:
        return loss_fn(score, u_t, t)
    half = len(x1) // 2
    negatives = torch.cat([
        langevin_sweep(model, x0[:half], n_steps=LANGEVIN_STEPS),
        langevin_hold(model, x1[half:], n_steps=LANGEVIN_STEPS),
    ])
    energy_pos, _ = model(x1)
    energy_neg, _ = model(negatives)
    return loss_fn(score, u_t, t, energy_pos, energy_neg)


for phase, n_steps in ((1, FLOW_STEPS), (2, JOINT_STEPS)):
    for step in range(n_steps):
        batch = data[torch.randint(len(data), (128,), device=device)]
        loss = compute_loss(batch, contrastive=phase == 2)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        progress(f"phase {phase}", step, n_steps, loss)

temperature = TemperatureScheduler(
    epsilon_max=EPS_MAX, tau_star=TAU_STAR, n_steps=SWEEP_STEPS, t_end=1.0
)
sampler = LangevinDynamics(step_size=DT, noise_scale=temperature)
samples = sampler(model, torch.randn(4000, 2, device=device), n_steps=SWEEP_STEPS)


def moon_distance(p):
    """Distance to the nearest point of the two analytic moon arcs."""
    dists = []
    for cx, cy, upper in ((0.0, 0.0, True), (1.0, 0.5, False)):
        v = p - torch.tensor([cx, cy], device=p.device)
        ang = torch.atan2(v[:, 1], v[:, 0])
        ang = ang.clamp(0.0, torch.pi) if upper else ang.clamp(-torch.pi, 0.0)
        arc = torch.stack([ang.cos() + cx, ang.sin() + cy], dim=-1)
        dists.append((p - arc).norm(dim=1))
    return torch.stack(dists, dim=1).min(dim=1)


near = moon_distance(samples)
outer = (near.indices == 0).float().mean()
print(
    f"median distance to moons: {near.values.median():.3f}"
    f"  within 0.15: {(near.values < 0.15).float().mean():.1%}"
    f"  outer/inner split: {outer:.1%}/{1 - outer:.1%}"
)

docs.title: Energy Matching: the paper's 2D suite
docs.text:
advanced · Reproduce the paper's toy experiments end to end: 8 Gaussians transported onto two moons, with trajectories, sample evolution, LID estimation, and repulsive diverse sampling.

Run it:

python examples/20-training/04-energy-matching/02-energy-matching-paper-2d/main.py

Reproduces the 2D experiments of Energy Matching (arXiv:2504.10612) on the paper's own toy datasets: a single time-independent potential \(V(x)\) transports an 8-Gaussian ring onto two moons, then samples its Boltzmann density near the data. main.py trains with live terminal progress and prints the quantitative checks; plot.py renders the figures.

plot.py renders four figures locally (they are not committed):

  • Sample evolution along the SDE sweep: deterministic transport below \(\tau^*\), Langevin ramp after.
  • The two-regime schedule: temperature \(\epsilon(t)\) and the flow-loss time gate \(w(t)\).
  • Local intrinsic dimension: the Hessian of \(V\) at data points has one flat (tangent) and one stiff (normal) direction, so \(\mathrm{LID} = d - \mathrm{rank}(\nabla^2 V) \approx 1\) on the moons.
  • Diverse generation: 64 Langevin chains started from a single point, without and with the paper's repulsive interaction energy \(W\).
"""Energy Matching paper suite: 8 Gaussians -> Two Moons with diagnostics.

Reproduces the 2D experiments of arXiv:2504.10612 on the paper's own toy
datasets: an 8-Gaussian ring is transported onto two moons by one
time-independent potential V(x), trained with the two-phase EM recipe
(OT flow warm-up, then contrastive sharpening). Beyond generation quality,
this covers the paper's toy diagnostics: local intrinsic dimension from the
Hessian of V (their Sec. 3.3) and diverse sampling with the repulsive
interaction energy W, which fans 64 chains started from one data point out
along the manifold (the paper's inverse-design mechanism). Run plot.py
afterwards for the full figure suite.

Training calls the model for (V(x), -grad V(x)) at once; afterwards it
switches to its energy view, which the samplers differentiate, the Hessian
diagnostics read directly and InteractionModel wraps. Generation is one SDE
sweep t: 0 -> 1 started from the source distribution.

A GPU is recommended (~8 minutes end to end; CPU is much slower).
"""

import math
import os

import torch
from torch import nn
from torch.func import hessian, vmap

from torchebm.core import BaseModel, TemperatureScheduler
from torchebm.couplings import SinkhornCoupling
from torchebm.datasets import GaussianMixtureDataset, TwoMoonsDataset
from torchebm.interpolants import LinearInterpolant
from torchebm.losses import EnergyMatchingLoss
from torchebm.models import InteractionModel
from torchebm.samplers import LangevinDynamics


class MLP(BaseModel):
    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(2, 256), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 256), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 256), nn.SiLU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 1),
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x).squeeze(-1)


def progress(label, step, total, loss):
    """Inline terminal progress bar (stdlib only)."""
    if step % 100 and step != total - 1:
        return
    bar = "=" * int(30 * (step + 1) / total)
    end = "\n" if step == total - 1 else ""
    print(
        f"\r{label} [{bar:<30}] {step + 1:5d}/{total}  loss {loss.item():.4f}",
        end=end, flush=True,
    )


def moon_distance(p):
    """Distance to the nearest point of the two analytic moon arcs."""
    dists = []
    for cx, cy, upper in ((0.0, 0.0, True), (1.0, 0.5, False)):
        v = p - torch.tensor([cx, cy], device=p.device)
        ang = torch.atan2(v[:, 1], v[:, 0])
        ang = ang.clamp(0.0, torch.pi) if upper else ang.clamp(-torch.pi, 0.0)
        arc = torch.stack([ang.cos() + cx, ang.sin() + cy], dim=-1)
        dists.append((p - arc).norm(dim=1))
    return torch.stack(dists, dim=1).min(dim=1)


SMOKE = os.getenv("TORCHEBM_SMOKE") == "1"
FLOW_STEPS, JOINT_STEPS = (20, 5) if SMOKE else (20000, 2000)
LANGEVIN_STEPS = 10 if SMOKE else 200
SWEEP_STEPS = 20 if SMOKE else 200
EPS_MAX, TAU_STAR, DT = 0.15, 0.8, 0.01

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

source = GaussianMixtureDataset(
    n_samples=8000, n_components=8, std=0.1, radius=2.5, seed=0, device=device
).get_data()
target = TwoMoonsDataset(n_samples=8000, noise=0.05, seed=1, device=device).get_data()

model = MLP(prediction_type=("energy", "score")).to(device)
coupling = SinkhornCoupling(reg=0.01)
path = LinearInterpolant()
loss_fn = EnergyMatchingLoss(lambda_cd=2.0, cd_trim_fraction=0.0, cd_clamp=None)
langevin_sweep = LangevinDynamics(
    step_size=DT,
    noise_scale=TemperatureScheduler(
        epsilon_max=EPS_MAX, tau_star=TAU_STAR, n_steps=LANGEVIN_STEPS
    ),
)
langevin_hold = LangevinDynamics(step_size=DT, noise_scale=math.sqrt(EPS_MAX))
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-4)


def next_batch():
    i1 = torch.randint(len(target), (128,), device=device)
    i0 = torch.randint(len(source), (128,), device=device)
    return target[i1], source[i0]


def compute_loss(x1, x0, contrastive):
    x0, x1 = coupling(x0, x1)
    t = torch.rand(len(x1), device=device)
    x_t, u_t = path(x0, x1, t)
    x_t = x_t + 0.1 * torch.randn_like(x_t)
    _, score = model(x_t)
    if not contrastive:
        return loss_fn(score, u_t, t)
    half = len(x1) // 2
    negatives = torch.cat([
        langevin_sweep(model, x0[:half], n_steps=LANGEVIN_STEPS),
        langevin_hold(model, x1[half:], n_steps=LANGEVIN_STEPS),
    ])
    energy_pos, _ = model(x1)
    energy_neg, _ = model(negatives)
    return loss_fn(score, u_t, t, energy_pos, energy_neg)


for step in range(FLOW_STEPS):
    x1, x0 = next_batch()
    loss = compute_loss(x1, x0, contrastive=False)
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    progress("phase 1 (OT flow)", step, FLOW_STEPS, loss)

for step in range(JOINT_STEPS):
    x1, x0 = next_batch()
    loss = compute_loss(x1, x0, contrastive=True)
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    progress("phase 2 (EM)     ", step, JOINT_STEPS, loss)

model.prediction_type = "energy"

temperature = TemperatureScheduler(
    epsilon_max=EPS_MAX, tau_star=TAU_STAR, n_steps=SWEEP_STEPS, t_end=1.0
)
sampler = LangevinDynamics(step_size=DT, noise_scale=temperature)
x_init = source[torch.randperm(len(source), device=device)[:4000]]
samples = sampler(model, x_init, n_steps=SWEEP_STEPS)

near = moon_distance(samples)
outer = (near.indices == 0).float().mean()
print(
    f"transport 8 Gaussians -> moons: median distance {near.values.median():.3f}"
    f"  within 0.15: {(near.values < 0.15).float().mean():.1%}"
    f"  outer/inner split: {outer:.1%}/{1 - outer:.1%}"
)


def hessian_eigs(points):
    """Eigenvalues of the Hessian of V at `points`.

    LID = d - rank(grad^2 V): flat (small-eigenvalue) directions are tangent to
    the manifold. The rank uses a per-point relative threshold and is
    meaningful on the density ridge, where V is convex. The moons are curves,
    so the true LID is 1.
    """
    v_single = lambda p: model(p.unsqueeze(0)).squeeze(0)
    return torch.linalg.eigvalsh(vmap(hessian(v_single))(points)).detach()


eig_data = hessian_eigs(target[:512])
rank = (eig_data > 0.3 * eig_data[:, 1:].clamp(min=1e-6)).sum(dim=1)
lid_data = 2.0 - rank.float()
x_random = torch.rand(512, 2, device=device) * 4.0 - torch.tensor([1.5, 1.5], device=device)
eig_random = hessian_eigs(x_random)
print(
    f"LID at data points: mean {lid_data.mean():.2f} (true manifold dim: 1)"
    f"   stiff-eigenvalue medians: data {eig_data[:, 1].median():.1f}"
    f" vs off-manifold {eig_random[:, 1].median():.1f}"
)

x_seed = target[:1].expand(64, -1).contiguous()
samples_plain = langevin_hold(model, x_seed, n_steps=SWEEP_STEPS)
interaction_model = InteractionModel(model, sigma_w=4.0, strength=0.15)
samples_repulsive = langevin_hold(interaction_model, x_seed, n_steps=SWEEP_STEPS)


def mean_pairwise(x):
    return torch.pdist(x).mean()


print(
    f"diversity (mean pairwise distance) from one seed point:"
    f"  plain {mean_pairwise(samples_plain):.2f}"
    f"  vs  repulsive {mean_pairwise(samples_repulsive):.2f}"
)

docs.title: Coupling Comparison
docs.text:
intermediate · Independent, greedy, Sinkhorn, and exact OT pairings on the same batch; transport cost and per-pair weights.

Run it:

python examples/20-training/05-couplings/01-coupling-comparison/main.py

"""Couplings: how noise is paired with data before interpolation.

The coupling decides which x0 trains against which x1; straighter pairings mean
straighter probability paths and fewer sampling steps downstream.

    cost = E ||x1 - x0||^2 under the pairing

A CouplingResult unpacks as the pair (x0, x1); extras such as the per-pair
weights of unbalanced OT, which relaxes the marginal constraints and reweights
the pairs, ride on it as attributes and go to the loss's weight= argument. In
a training loop the coupling runs right before the interpolant:

    x0, x1 = coupling(x0, x1)
    x_t, u_t = path(x0, x1, t)
"""

import torch

from torchebm.couplings import (
    ExactOTCoupling,
    GreedyCoupling,
    IndependentCoupling,
    SinkhornCoupling,
    UnbalancedSinkhornCoupling,
)
from torchebm.datasets import TwoMoonsDataset

torch.manual_seed(0)
x0 = torch.randn(512, 2)
x1 = TwoMoonsDataset(n_samples=512, noise=0.05, seed=0).get_data()


def cost(a, b):
    return ((b - a) ** 2).sum(-1).mean()


couplings = {
    "independent": IndependentCoupling(),
    "greedy": GreedyCoupling(),
    "sinkhorn (reg=0.05)": SinkhornCoupling(reg=0.05),
    "exact OT": ExactOTCoupling(),
}

print(f"{'coupling':22s} E||x1 - x0||^2")
for name, coupling in couplings.items():
    x0_paired, x1_paired = coupling(x0, x1)
    print(f"{name:22s} {cost(x0_paired, x1_paired):.3f}")

result = UnbalancedSinkhornCoupling(reg=0.05, reg_marginal=1.0)(x0, x1)
weights = result.weights
print(f"unbalanced sinkhorn    {cost(result.x0, result.x1):.3f}"
      f"   weights: min {weights.min():.2f} max {weights.max():.2f} (uniform would be 1.0)")

docs.title: Flow Matching in 2D
docs.text:
beginner · Train a time-conditioned velocity field with FlowMatchingLoss and integrate it noise-to-data with FlowSampler, comparing the adaLN-Zero and concat conditioning of TimeConditionedMLP.

Run it:

python examples/20-training/06-flow-matching/01-flow-matching-2d/main.py

"""Flow Matching in 2D: regress a velocity field, integrate it to sample.

Conditional flow matching draws (x0, x1) pairs from noise and data, places
x_t on the interpolant between them, and regresses the model onto the
interpolant velocity u_t:

    L = || v(x_t, t) - u_t ||^2

The interpolant builds (x_t, u_t) in the loop, the loss compares the model
output with u_t. Sampling integrates the learned velocity forward from noise
with FlowSampler (the field points noise -> data).

The model is TimeConditionedMLP, which carries DiT's adaLN-Zero conditioning
on a vector stream by default; conditioning="concat" is the hand-rolled
[x, t_emb] baseline seen in most tutorials. Both train here for comparison.
"""

import os

import torch

from torchebm.datasets import TwoMoonsDataset
from torchebm.interpolants import LinearInterpolant
from torchebm.losses import FlowMatchingLoss
from torchebm.models import TimeConditionedMLP
from torchebm.samplers import FlowSampler

SMOKE = os.getenv("TORCHEBM_SMOKE") == "1"
N_STEPS = 20 if SMOKE else 3000
N_GEN = 128 if SMOKE else 2000


def train(conditioning):
    """Train a velocity field on two-moons with the given conditioning mode."""
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    data = TwoMoonsDataset(n_samples=4000, noise=0.05, seed=0).get_data()
    model = TimeConditionedMLP(in_dim=2, conditioning=conditioning)
    path = LinearInterpolant()
    loss_fn = FlowMatchingLoss()
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    for _ in range(N_STEPS):
        x1 = data[torch.randint(len(data), (256,))]
        x0 = torch.randn_like(x1)
        t = torch.rand(len(x1))
        x_t, u_t = path(x0, x1, t)
        loss = loss_fn(model(x_t, t), u_t)
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
    return model, data


def median_dist(samples, data):
    """Median distance from each sample to the nearest data point."""
    return torch.cdist(samples, data).min(dim=1).values.median().item()


torch.manual_seed(1)
x0 = torch.randn(N_GEN, 2)

for conditioning in ("adaln_zero", "concat"):
    model, data = train(conditioning)
    samples = FlowSampler(integrator="euler")(model, x0, n_steps=100)
    print(f"{conditioning:11s} median dist to data: {median_dist(samples, data):.3f}")

docs.title: Density Transport
docs.text:
intermediate · salvage · Treat an image as a Boltzmann density and assemble it from noise with annealed Langevin dynamics.

Run it:

python examples/90-showcase/01-density-transport/main.py

Treat an ordinary image as an unnormalised probability density and watch a cloud of noise particles assemble into it under annealed Langevin dynamics, sampled with TorchEBM's LangevinDynamics through a custom BaseModel energy.

docs.title: What it teaches
docs.text:
• An image's pixel intensity defines a Boltzmann density \(p(x) \propto \rho(x)\), so the energy is \(E(x) = -\log \rho(x)\). A differentiable bilinear lookup (grid_sample) lets autograd supply the score \(\nabla_x \log \rho(x)\) that the sampler follows.
  • Coarse-to-fine annealing, blur the density then sharpen it in stages, gives broad basins of attraction first and crisp detail last. This is the intuition behind annealed Langevin and score-based generative sampling, applied to a real image.

docs.title: Requires
docs.text: In addition to TorchEBM, this showcase needs Pillow: pip install pillow.

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
One GIF per --target, written to the assets/ folder next to the script (density_transport_<target>.gif), showing a cloud of particles transported from noise into the target image (logo, galaxy, neuron, starry_night).

r"""
Density transport animation for TorchEBM.

An image is treated as an unnormalised target density: pixel intensity defines
a Boltzmann density p(x) \propto rho(x), so the energy is E(x) = -log rho(x).
A cloud of particles initialised as Gaussian noise is transported into the
target by Langevin dynamics, sampled with TorchEBM's own `LangevinDynamics`
through a `BaseModel` energy. Sampling is annealed coarse-to-fine: the density
starts heavily blurred (broad basins of attraction) and is sharpened in stages,
which mirrors annealed Langevin / score-based sampling and yields a clean
assembly of fine detail.

This is the intuition behind score-based generative sampling, applied to a real
image. `--target` selects one of the bundled targets: public-domain or freely
licensed Wikimedia images, fetched through the Special:FilePath redirect.
Outputs land next to this script (assets/ is gitignored for examples).

Run:
    python examples/90-showcase/01-density-transport/main.py --target logo
    python examples/90-showcase/01-density-transport/main.py --target galaxy
    python examples/90-showcase/01-density-transport/main.py --target neuron
    python examples/90-showcase/01-density-transport/main.py --target starry_night
    python examples/90-showcase/01-density-transport/main.py --target all
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.animation import FuncAnimation, PillowWriter
from PIL import Image, ImageFilter

from torchebm.core import BaseModel
from torchebm.samplers.langevin_dynamics import LangevinDynamics

OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "assets"
CACHE = OUT / "_targets"
CACHE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

_UA = "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) torchebm-density-transport"

_FP = "https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:FilePath/"
REMOTE = {
    "galaxy": _FP + "NGC_4414_%28NASA-med%29.jpg?width=720",
    "neuron": _FP + "GFPneuron.png?width=720",
    "starry_night": _FP + "Van_Gogh_-_Starry_Night_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg?width=900",
}

GRID = 256


def _download(url: str, dst: Path) -> Path:
    if dst.exists():
        return dst
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": _UA})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as r:
        dst.write_bytes(r.read())
    return dst


def _render_wordmark() -> Image.Image:
    """Render the ' ∇ TorchEBM ' wordmark to a grayscale image via matplotlib."""
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(6, 6), dpi=GRID // 6)
    fig.patch.set_facecolor("black")
    ax = fig.add_axes([0, 0, 1, 1])
    ax.set_facecolor("black")
    ax.axis("off")
    ax.text(
        0.5, 0.60, r"$\nabla$", color="white", fontsize=104,
        ha="center", va="center", fontweight="bold",
    )
    ax.text(
        0.5, 0.30, "TorchEBM", color="white", fontsize=58,
        ha="center", va="center", fontweight="bold", family="DejaVu Sans",
    )
    fig.canvas.draw()
    w, h = fig.canvas.get_width_height()
    buf = np.frombuffer(fig.canvas.buffer_rgba(), dtype=np.uint8).reshape(h, w, 4)
    plt.close(fig)
    return Image.fromarray(buf[..., :3]).convert("L")


def load_density(target: str) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return a (GRID, GRID) float array in [0, 1]; bright = high density.

    Every bundled target reads as bright-on-dark already. Contrast is
    normalised, a gamma of 2.2 deepens the background and sharpens the
    subject, a tiny floor keeps the background pulling weakly, and the array
    is flipped so image row 0 (top) maps to +y (math convention).
    """
    if target == "logo":
        img = _render_wordmark()
    else:
        if target not in REMOTE:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown target {target!r}")
        path = _download(REMOTE[target], CACHE / f"{target}.img")
        img = Image.open(path).convert("L")

    img = img.resize((GRID, GRID), Image.LANCZOS)
    a = np.asarray(img, dtype=np.float32) / 255.0
    a = (a - a.min()) / (a.max() - a.min() + 1e-8)
    a = np.power(a, 2.2)
    a = 0.0015 + 0.9985 * a
    return np.flipud(a).copy()


def blurred(density: np.ndarray, sigma_px: float) -> np.ndarray:
    if sigma_px <= 0:
        return density
    img = Image.fromarray((density * 255).astype(np.uint8))
    img = img.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(radius=sigma_px))
    out = np.asarray(img, dtype=np.float32) / 255.0
    return (0.0015 + 0.9985 * (out - out.min()) / (out.max() - out.min() + 1e-8))


class ImageDensity(BaseModel):
    r"""Energy E(x) = -log rho(x) from an image density via bilinear sampling.

    The density grid is held as a (1, 1, H, W) buffer. For a batch of points in
    the box [-1, 1]^2, `grid_sample` performs a differentiable bilinear lookup,
    so autograd supplies the score \nabla_x log rho(x) that the sampler needs.
    """

    def __init__(self, density: np.ndarray, temperature: float = 1.0):
        super().__init__()
        grid = torch.from_numpy(density).float()[None, None]
        self.register_buffer("grid", grid)
        self.temperature = float(temperature)

    def set_density(self, density: np.ndarray) -> None:
        self.grid.copy_(torch.from_numpy(density).float()[None, None].to(self.grid))

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        n = x.shape[0]
        samp = x.view(1, n, 1, 2)
        dens = F.grid_sample(
            self.grid, samp, mode="bilinear",
            padding_mode="border", align_corners=True,
        ).view(n)
        return -torch.log(dens.clamp_min(1e-6)) / self.temperature


def transport(density: np.ndarray, device: str, n_particles: int = 11000):
    """Return a (frames, n_particles, 2) trajectory of the assembling cloud.

    Coarse-to-fine stages of (blur in px, step_size, noise_scale, steps, thin):
    the first, heavily blurred stage gives a global basin so particles anywhere
    in the box are pulled toward the subject; later stages sharpen onto detail
    while the noise is annealed toward near-zero for a crisp settle. The cloud
    starts uniform across the box so it visibly assembles from noise.
    """
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    model = ImageDensity(blurred(density, 36.0)).to(device)
    stages = [
        (36.0, 9e-3, 0.85, 200, 4),
        (16.0, 5e-3, 0.6, 200, 4),
        (7.0, 2.5e-3, 0.4, 220, 4),
        (3.0, 1.2e-3, 0.24, 240, 4),
        (1.2, 6e-4, 0.12, 260, 4),
        (0.5, 3e-4, 0.05, 300, 4),
    ]

    x = 2.0 * torch.rand(n_particles, 2, device=device) - 1.0
    frames = [x.cpu().numpy().copy()]

    for sigma, step_size, noise_scale, n_steps, thin in stages:
        model.set_density(blurred(density, sigma))
        sampler = LangevinDynamics(step_size=step_size, noise_scale=noise_scale)
        trajectory = sampler(model, x, n_steps=n_steps, return_trajectory=True)
        trajectory = trajectory[:, thin - 1 :: thin].clamp_(-1, 1)
        for k in range(trajectory.shape[1]):
            frames.append(trajectory[:, k].cpu().numpy().copy())
        x = trajectory[:, -1].contiguous()

    return np.stack(frames, axis=0)


def render(frames: np.ndarray, density: np.ndarray, out_path: Path, title: str):
    """Dark theme: glowing particles over the faint target as a guide rail,
    brightening as the cloud settles."""
    plt.rcParams.update({
        "font.family": "DejaVu Sans",
        "figure.facecolor": "#0b0b0f",
        "savefig.facecolor": "#0b0b0f",
    })
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 6.4), dpi=170)
    fig.subplots_adjust(0, 0, 1, 1)
    ax.set_facecolor("#0b0b0f")
    ax.set_xlim(-1, 1)
    ax.set_ylim(-1, 1)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.axis("off")

    ax.imshow(
        density, extent=(-1, 1, -1, 1), origin="lower",
        cmap="magma", alpha=0.22, zorder=0, interpolation="bilinear",
    )

    scat = ax.scatter(
        frames[0][:, 0], frames[0][:, 1], s=1.6, c="#ffd27f",
        alpha=0.5, linewidths=0, zorder=2,
    )
    tag = ax.text(
        0.5, 0.045, title, transform=ax.transAxes, color="#f5f5f7",
        ha="center", va="center", fontsize=15, fontweight="bold", alpha=0.92,
    )
    sub = ax.text(
        0.5, 0.012, "Langevin transport into an image density · TorchEBM",
        transform=ax.transAxes, color="#9aa0aa", ha="center", va="center",
        fontsize=8.5,
    )

    n = len(frames)

    def update(i):
        pts = frames[i]
        scat.set_offsets(pts)
        prog = i / (n - 1)
        scat.set_alpha(0.4 + 0.35 * prog)
        return scat, tag, sub

    anim = FuncAnimation(fig, update, frames=n, interval=40, blit=False)
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    anim.save(out_path, writer=PillowWriter(fps=25))
    plt.close(fig)
    print(f"wrote {out_path}  ({n} frames)")


TITLES = {
    "logo": "∇ TorchEBM",
    "galaxy": "NGC 4414",
    "neuron": "Cortical neuron",
    "starry_night": "The Starry Night",
}


def run(target: str, device: str):
    density = load_density(target)
    frames = transport(density, device=device)
    render(frames, density, OUT / f"density_transport_{target}.gif", TITLES[target])


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument(
        "--target",
        default="logo",
        choices=["logo", "galaxy", "neuron", "starry_night", "all"],
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--device",
        default="cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu",
    )
    args = p.parse_args()

    targets = ["logo", "galaxy", "neuron", "starry_night"] if args.target == "all" else [args.target]
    for t in targets:
        run(t, args.device)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Integrators vs. the Exact Solution
docs.text:
advanced · salvage · Race Euler, Heun, RK4 and the generalised leapfrog against ground truth on an ODE and a curved manifold.

Run it:

python examples/90-showcase/02-integrator-ode/main.py

Two time-series scenes that race TorchEBM's numerical integrators against a ground-truth solution, on the dark brand theme.

docs.title: What it teaches
docs.text:
• Order of accuracy (oscillator scene): on the undamped oscillator \(\ddot q = -q\), forward EulerMaruyamaIntegrator does not conserve energy and visibly drifts, while HeunIntegrator (2nd) and RK4Integrator (4th) stay on the exact \(\cos t\) curve.
  • Geometry-aware integration (riemannian scene): on a non-separable Hamiltonian with metric \(M(x)=1+x^2\), the standard LeapfrogIntegrator ignores the metric and integrates the wrong dynamics, while the new GeneralisedLeapfrogIntegrator solves the implicit, geometry-aware updates and tracks the reference. This is the rm-HMC setting that motivated the generalised integrator in v0.6.0.

docs.title: Requires
docs.text: Runs on TorchEBM alone. For the polished outputs, MP4 export uses imageio-ffmpeg and the brand logo uses cairosvg (pip install imageio-ffmpeg cairosvg); both degrade gracefully (GIF fallback, text title) when absent.

docs.title: Expected output
docs.text:
integrator_ode.{mp4,gif} (oscillator) and integrator_rmhmc.{mp4,gif} (riemannian), written to the assets/ folder next to the script; add --still for a final-frame PNG.

r"""Integrators vs. the exact solution: TorchEBM v0.6.0 announcement animations.

Two NeurIPS-style time-series scenes that race TorchEBM's numerical integrators
against a ground-truth solution, rendered on the dark brand theme.

scene "oscillator"  (default ground-truth = analytic cos t)
    The undamped harmonic oscillator  q'' = -q  (q(0)=1, p(0)=0, exact q=cos t).
    Forward Euler (1st), Heun (2nd) and RK4 (4th) are driven step-by-step; Euler
    does not conserve energy and visibly drifts while the higher-order methods
    stay on the exact curve, the classic order-of-accuracy picture.

scene "riemannian"  (ground-truth = an independent fine-step RK4 reference)
    A *non-separable* Hamiltonian with a position-dependent metric M(x)=1+x^2
    (the Riemann-manifold-HMC setting, Girolami & Calderhead 2011). The standard
    LeapfrogIntegrator assumes a separable Hamiltonian, so it ignores the metric
    and integrates the wrong dynamics; the new GeneralisedLeapfrogIntegrator
    solves the implicit, geometry-aware updates and tracks the reference. This is
    why TorchEBM 0.6.0 adds the generalised integrator.

Every plotted curve is the per-step output of the integrator (the
``integrate`` methods return only the final state, so we drive ``step`` directly).

Run both scenes (MP4 and GIF), one scene with a still frame, or one scene
without the GIF:
    python examples/90-showcase/02-integrator-ode/main.py
    python examples/90-showcase/02-integrator-ode/main.py --scene riemannian --still
    python examples/90-showcase/02-integrator-ode/main.py --scene oscillator --no-gif
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import math
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch
import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patheffects as pe
from matplotlib.animation import FuncAnimation, PillowWriter

from torchebm.integrators import (
    EulerMaruyamaIntegrator,
    HeunIntegrator,
    RK4Integrator,
    LeapfrogIntegrator,
    GeneralisedLeapfrogIntegrator,
)

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "assets"
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

LOGO_SVG = ROOT / "docs" / "assets" / "images" / "logo_with_text.svg"
LOGO_PNG = OUT / "_targets" / "logo_with_text.png"

BG = "#0b0b0f"
FG = "#f5f5f7"
MUTED = "#9aa0aa"
LIME = "#C7FF00"
TRUTH = "#e8e8ee"
ORANGE = "#E69F00"
BLUE = "#56B4E9"
GREEN = "#00D49A"


def osc_drift(x: torch.Tensor, t: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Autonomous drift f(z) = (p, -q) for the unit harmonic oscillator."""
    q, p = x[..., 0], x[..., 1]
    return torch.stack([p, -q], dim=-1)


def osc_run(integrator, x0: torch.Tensor, h: float, n_steps: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Advance one RK integrator step-by-step; return the q-trajectory."""
    state = {"x": x0.clone()}
    qs = [float(x0[..., 0].item())]
    for i in range(n_steps):
        state = integrator.step(state, h, drift=osc_drift, t=torch.full((1,), i * h))
        qs.append(float(state["x"][..., 0].item()))
    return np.asarray(qs, dtype=np.float64)


def build_oscillator(h: float, periods: float) -> dict:
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    x0 = torch.tensor([[1.0, 0.0]])
    n = int(round(periods * 2 * math.pi / h))
    t = np.arange(n + 1, dtype=np.float64) * h
    exact = np.cos(t)

    methods = [
        ("Euler · 1st order", ORANGE, EulerMaruyamaIntegrator, 3.2, 4, True),
        ("Heun · 2nd order", BLUE, HeunIntegrator, 3.4, 6, True),
        ("RK4 · 4th order", GREEN, RK4Integrator, 1.9, 7, False),
    ]
    series = []
    rows = []
    for label, color, builder, lw, z, glow in methods:
        q = osc_run(builder(), x0, h, n)
        series.append({"label": label, "color": color, "traj": q,
                       "lw": lw, "z": z, "glow": glow})
        rows.append((label, abs(q[-1]), float(np.max(np.abs(q - exact)))))
    _print_table("harmonic oscillator  q''=-q", h, n, t[-1], t[-1] / (2 * math.pi), rows)

    return {
        "t": t, "ref": exact, "ref_label": "exact  cos(t)", "series": series,
        "ylim": 2.9, "ylabel": "position  q(t)",
        "subtitle": r"Numerical integrators vs. the exact solution  ·  $\ddot{q}=-q$",
        "out": "integrator_ode",
    }


RM_PERIOD = 8.0


def rm_force(x, p, t):
    invM = 1.0 / (1.0 + x ** 2)
    return -(x + 0.5 * p ** 2 * (-2.0 * x * invM ** 2) + 0.5 * (2.0 * x * invM))


def rm_velocity(x, p, t):
    return p / (1.0 + x ** 2)


def rm_full_drift(z, t):
    """First-order field (velocity, force) for the independent RK4 reference."""
    x, p = z[..., 0:1], z[..., 1:2]
    return torch.cat([rm_velocity(x, p, t), rm_force(x, p, t)], dim=-1)


def _rm_x0(x0, p0):
    return torch.tensor([[x0]]), torch.tensor([[p0]])


def rm_generalised(x0, p0, h, n) -> np.ndarray:
    integ = GeneralisedLeapfrogIntegrator()
    x, p = _rm_x0(x0, p0)
    state = {"x": x, "p": p}
    xs = [float(x0)]
    for _ in range(n):
        state = integ.step(state, h, force=rm_force, velocity=rm_velocity)
        xs.append(float(state["x"].item()))
    return np.asarray(xs, dtype=np.float64)


def rm_leapfrog(x0, p0, h, n) -> np.ndarray:
    integ = LeapfrogIntegrator()
    x, p = _rm_x0(x0, p0)
    state = {"x": x, "p": p}
    xs = [float(x0)]
    for _ in range(n):
        state = integ.step(state, h, drift=lambda x, t: -x)
        xs.append(float(state["x"].item()))
    return np.asarray(xs, dtype=np.float64)


def rm_reference(x0, p0, h, n) -> np.ndarray:
    integ = RK4Integrator()
    state = {"x": torch.tensor([[x0, p0]])}
    xs = [float(x0)]
    for _ in range(n):
        state = integ.step(state, h, drift=rm_full_drift)
        xs.append(float(state["x"][..., 0].item()))
    return np.asarray(xs, dtype=np.float64)


def build_riemannian(h: float, periods: float) -> dict:
    """Non-separable Hamiltonian with metric M(x) = 1 + x^2 and U(x) = x^2 / 2.

    Standard Leapfrog sees only drift = -dU/dx and unit mass, so it integrates
    the wrong dynamics; GeneralisedLeapfrog takes (force, velocity) and is
    exact for the metric. RM_PERIOD is the measured period of the reference
    orbit from (x0, p0) = (1.6, 0); the reference is an independent fine-step
    RK4 run.
    """
    x0, p0 = 1.6, 0.0
    n = int(round(periods * RM_PERIOD / h))
    t = np.arange(n + 1, dtype=np.float64) * h

    sub = 20
    ref = rm_reference(x0, p0, h / sub, n * sub)[::sub]
    glf = rm_generalised(x0, p0, h, n)
    lf = rm_leapfrog(x0, p0, h, n)

    rows = [("GeneralisedLeapfrog", abs(glf[-1]), float(np.max(np.abs(glf - ref)))),
            ("Leapfrog", abs(lf[-1]), float(np.max(np.abs(lf - ref))))]
    _print_table("non-separable H  ·  M(x)=1+x^2", h, n, t[-1], t[-1] / RM_PERIOD, rows,
                 errlabel="max err vs ref")

    series = [
        {"label": "GeneralisedLeapfrog · respects M(x)", "color": GREEN, "traj": glf,
         "lw": 2.6, "z": 7, "glow": True},
        {"label": "Leapfrog · ignores the metric", "color": ORANGE, "traj": lf,
         "lw": 2.8, "z": 5, "glow": True},
    ]
    return {
        "t": t, "ref": ref, "ref_label": "reference  ·  fine RK4", "series": series,
        "ylim": 1.95, "ylabel": "position  x(t)",
        "subtitle": r"Geometry-aware integration  ·  non-separable $H$,  $M(x)=1+x^2$",
        "out": "integrator_rmhmc",
    }


def _print_table(title, h, n, T, periods, rows, errlabel="max abs err"):
    print(f"\n  {title}   h={h}  n_steps={n}  T={T:.2f}  ({periods:.2f} periods)")
    print(f"  {'method':<24}{'end |x|':>10}{errlabel:>16}")
    print("  " + "-" * 50)
    for name, end, err in rows:
        print(f"  {name:<24}{end:>10.3f}{err:>16.3e}")
    print()


def _glow(lw: float, color: str, alpha: float = 0.35):
    """Soft outer glow so semi-thick lines pop on the dark background."""
    return [pe.Stroke(linewidth=lw + 3.5, foreground=color, alpha=alpha), pe.Normal()]


def load_logo(width_px: int = 1400):
    """Return the brand wordmark as a trimmed RGBA array (or None).

    Rasterizes the canonical ``logo_with_text.svg`` with cairosvg (cached under
    ``_targets/``) so the logo is always the real one. Falls back to the cached
    PNG, then to ``None`` (caller draws a text title instead).
    """
    try:
        import cairosvg
        LOGO_PNG.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        cairosvg.svg2png(url=str(LOGO_SVG), write_to=str(LOGO_PNG), output_width=width_px)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        print(f"  (cairosvg unavailable: {exc}; using cached logo if present)")
    if not LOGO_PNG.exists():
        return None
    from PIL import Image
    im = Image.open(LOGO_PNG).convert("RGBA")
    bbox = im.getbbox()
    return np.asarray(im.crop(bbox) if bbox else im)


def _draw_header(fig, subtitle: str):
    """The SVG wordmark with the version snug to its right, plus a subtitle."""
    lx, lcy, logo_h = 0.088, 0.945, 0.056
    logo = load_logo()
    if logo is not None:
        aspect = logo.shape[1] / logo.shape[0]
        logo_w = logo_h * aspect
        logo_ax = fig.add_axes([lx, lcy - logo_h / 2, logo_w, logo_h], zorder=6)
        logo_ax.imshow(logo, aspect="auto", interpolation="antialiased")
        logo_ax.axis("off")
        logo_ax.patch.set_visible(False)
        ver_x = lx + logo_w + 0.018
    else:
        fig.text(lx, lcy, "∇ TorchEBM", color=LIME, fontsize=23,
                 fontweight="bold", ha="left", va="center")
        ver_x = 0.50
    fig.text(ver_x, lcy, "0.6.0", color=FG, fontsize=22, fontweight="bold",
             ha="left", va="center", alpha=0.9)
    fig.text(lx, lcy - 0.052, subtitle, color=MUTED, fontsize=12.5,
             ha="left", va="center")


def render(scene: dict, *, fps: int, hold: int,
           make_mp4: bool, make_gif: bool, still: bool):
    plt.rcParams.update({
        "font.family": "DejaVu Sans",
        "figure.facecolor": BG, "savefig.facecolor": BG,
        "text.color": FG, "axes.edgecolor": MUTED,
    })

    t, ref, ylim = scene["t"], scene["ref"], scene["ylim"]
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 7.2), dpi=150)
    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.105, right=0.965, top=0.85, bottom=0.115)
    ax.set_facecolor(BG)
    ax.set_xlim(t[0], t[-1])
    ax.set_ylim(-ylim, ylim)
    ax.set_xlabel("time  t", color=MUTED, fontsize=12)
    ax.set_ylabel(scene["ylabel"], color=MUTED, fontsize=12)
    ax.tick_params(colors=MUTED, labelsize=10)
    for s in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
    for s in ("left", "bottom"):
        ax.spines[s].set_color(MUTED)
        ax.spines[s].set_alpha(0.4)
    ax.grid(True, color=MUTED, alpha=0.12, linewidth=0.8)
    ax.axhline(0.0, color=MUTED, alpha=0.18, linewidth=0.8)

    ax.plot(t, ref, color=TRUTH, lw=7.0, alpha=0.10, solid_capstyle="round", zorder=1)
    (ref_line,) = ax.plot([], [], color=TRUTH, lw=2.0, ls=(0, (5, 4)), alpha=0.9,
                          label=scene["ref_label"], zorder=8)

    lines, dots = [], []
    for spec in scene["series"]:
        (ln,) = ax.plot([], [], color=spec["color"], lw=spec["lw"],
                        solid_capstyle="round", label=spec["label"], zorder=spec["z"])
        if spec["glow"]:
            ln.set_path_effects(_glow(spec["lw"], spec["color"]))
        (dot,) = ax.plot([], [], "o", color=spec["color"], ms=6.0,
                         zorder=spec["z"] + 10, markeredgecolor=BG, markeredgewidth=1.0)
        lines.append((ln, spec["traj"]))
        dots.append(dot)

    ax.legend(loc="upper left", frameon=True, facecolor=BG, edgecolor="none",
              framealpha=0.6, fontsize=11, labelcolor=FG, handlelength=1.8,
              borderaxespad=0.6)
    _draw_header(fig, scene["subtitle"])
    fig.text(0.965, 0.04, "pip install torchebm", color=MUTED, fontsize=10,
             ha="right", va="center", alpha=0.8)

    n = len(t)

    def update(i):
        k = min(i, n - 1) + 1
        ref_line.set_data(t[:k], ref[:k])
        arts = [ref_line]
        for (ln, traj), dot in zip(lines, dots):
            ln.set_data(t[:k], traj[:k])
            dot.set_data([t[k - 1]], [traj[k - 1]])
            arts += [ln, dot]
        return arts

    total = n + hold
    anim = FuncAnimation(fig, update, frames=total, interval=1000 / fps, blit=False)
    base = OUT / scene["out"]

    if make_mp4:
        try:
            import imageio_ffmpeg
            plt.rcParams["animation.ffmpeg_path"] = imageio_ffmpeg.get_ffmpeg_exe()
            from matplotlib.animation import FFMpegWriter
            writer = FFMpegWriter(fps=fps, codec="libx264", bitrate=-1,
                                  extra_args=["-pix_fmt", "yuv420p", "-crf", "18",
                                              "-preset", "slow"])
            anim.save(base.with_suffix(".mp4"), writer=writer, dpi=150)
            print(f"wrote {base.with_suffix('.mp4')}  ({total} frames @ {fps}fps)")
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"!! MP4 export failed ({exc}); install imageio-ffmpeg. Falling back to GIF.")
            make_gif = True

    if make_gif:
        anim.save(base.with_suffix(".gif"), writer=PillowWriter(fps=min(fps, 25)), dpi=84)
        print(f"wrote {base.with_suffix('.gif')}  ({total} frames)")

    if still:
        update(n - 1)
        fig.savefig(base.with_suffix(".png"), dpi=150)
        print(f"wrote {base.with_suffix('.png')}")

    plt.close(fig)


SCENES = {"oscillator": build_oscillator, "riemannian": build_riemannian}
DEFAULT_H = {"oscillator": 0.13, "riemannian": 0.09}
DEFAULT_PERIODS = {"oscillator": 2.5, "riemannian": 3.0}


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    p.add_argument("--scene", choices=["oscillator", "riemannian", "both"], default="both")
    p.add_argument("--h", type=float, default=None, help="integrator step size (per-scene default)")
    p.add_argument("--periods", type=float, default=None, help="periods to show (per-scene default)")
    p.add_argument("--fps", type=int, default=30)
    p.add_argument("--hold", type=int, default=20, help="freeze frames at the end")
    p.add_argument("--no-mp4", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--no-gif", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--still", action="store_true", help="also save a final-frame PNG")
    args = p.parse_args()

    names = ["oscillator", "riemannian"] if args.scene == "both" else [args.scene]
    for name in names:
        h = args.h if args.h is not None else DEFAULT_H[name]
        periods = args.periods if args.periods is not None else DEFAULT_PERIODS[name]
        scene = SCENES[name](h, periods)
        render(scene, fps=args.fps, hold=args.hold,
               make_mp4=not args.no_mp4, make_gif=not args.no_gif, still=args.still)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

A short, narrated web animation comparing numerical integrators on an ODE, an SDE, and a curved manifold. TorchEBM is the compute engine; the browser only renders precomputed trajectories.

compute.py   → runs every experiment with TorchEBM → data.js (+ data.json, preview.png)
index.html   → the page
app.js       → renderer: Canvas2D (Ch.1–2) + Three.js (Ch.3) + narration timeline + recorder
vendor/      → three.min.js (r128, vendored so it works offline)

docs.title: Chapters
docs.text:
1. ODE: Kepler orbit. Forward Euler spirals out, RK4 slowly decays, symplectic Leapfrog holds a stable ellipse; an energy meter shows the drift.
  2. SDE: Langevin double-well. Walkers under dX = −∇U dt + √(2T) dW build a histogram that matches the true Boltzmann p ∝ e^(−U/T); all three SDE integrators agree.
  3. S²: geodesic. A naive flat-space Euler step drifts off the sphere, while an exponential-map (geodesic, Riemannian) step stays exact, as in RM-HMC and GeneralisedLeapfrog.

  • Record .webm captures the canvas to a video file. Convert it to mp4 with the ffmpeg binary bundled with imageio-ffmpeg; the first command prints its path: 
    python -c "import imageio_ffmpeg as f;print(f.get_ffmpeg_exe())"
<ffmpeg> -i torchebm_integrators.webm -pix_fmt yuv420p torchebm_integrators.mp4
